I'm 65 this year, and I've been farming these 2 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. Finished middle school back in the day, so I can read the fertilizer bags and do the math, but honestly, I trust what I see in the field more than what any book says. My wife passed away a few years back, and my son works in Shijiazhuang, so it's just me now. Two mu isn't much, but it's my land, and it keeps me fed with a bit left to sell.

It's early October, time to plant winter wheat. I've already had the tractor guy come rotavate both mu—cost me 40 yuan per mu. I saved some Jimai 22 seed from last year, but after three years the vigor drops, so this year I'll buy fresh seed. About 15 kg per mu at roughly 6 yuan per kg. The extension station says 12 kg per mu is enough, but I sow a bit thicker. At my age, I don't want to be out here re-planting if the stand is thin.

For fertilizer, I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting—that's the 15-15-15 type. Then come spring, around jointing in late March, I'll topdress with 13 kg of urea per mu if the wheat looks yellow. That works out to about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I know some neighbors put down 18 kg N, but fertilizer prices went up again, and with just this little plot and my pension, I need to watch every yuan. Still, I won't go below 10 kg N—I tried saving too much on fertilizer back in '98 and the yield crashed. I'd rather waste a little money than risk a bad year.

Irrigation—I'll water twice: once at jointing and once at grain filling. Pumping from the well costs electricity, and the bill adds up fast. Three times would be better, but unless it's a real drought spring, two is my limit.

For the summer maize, the window after wheat harvest in early June will be tight. I'll hire the planter crew—they charge about 30 yuan per mu, but at 65 I can't plant 2 mu by hand in two days. I'll buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958, about 3 jin per mu, costs around 45 yuan. For maize, I'll put 40 kg of compound at planting, and topdress with 10 kg urea at the big trumpet stage if I have time. That's about 11 kg N per mu. Maize is tougher than wheat, but I won't starve it either. If it's dry at flowering, I'll irrigate once. Herbicide for both crops, nothing else unless I see aphids.

Labor is mostly me. For wheat harvest I'll hire the combine—80 yuan per mu, non-negotiable, my back can't handle the sickle anymore. For maize harvest I'll do it myself with a small hand sheller, maybe hire one day of help to carry the sacks. I expect about 380 kg per mu for wheat and 400 kg per mu for maize. Last year was 370 and 410. I don't need records—I need stability.
